notes.block: Bengali-Assamese, U+0980-U+09FF. Words are runs of these letters and signs, ZWJ, ZWNJ, and apostrophes inside a word (হ'ল, ক'ত: Assamese marks the vowel o with one).
notes.notWord: Digits ০-৯ and the currency and fraction signs are not word letters; ৰ U+09F0 and ৱ U+09F1 are.
notes.replace: After NFC, before the engine's joiner rules: ত + virama + ZWJ is the old encoding of khanda ta ৎ; the Bengali ra র (U+09B0) is not an Assamese letter and is folded to ৰ (U+09F0), since Assamese text often has it from Bengali fonts and input methods (তোমার for তোমাৰ, প্রথম for প্ৰথম). ৰ, ৱ and ব are kept as they are. NFC leaves য়, ড়, ঢ় as base + nukta (U+09BC), since U+09DC/09DD/09DF are composition exclusions. Two mis-encodings common in the dumps are mended: া + ে (the halves of ো in visual order: মােৰ) becomes ো, and অ + া becomes আ (অাৰু).
notes.phraseBreaks: Assamese ends a sentence with the danda । (U+0964); ॥ ends verse, and ৷ (U+09F7) is often typed for a danda. Next-word pairs never span one.
notes.signs: A vowel sign or virama must follow a consonant or nukta (a base): a word with one after a vowel or another sign is mis-encoded text (আু, অৰুি) and is not counted.
